properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued November 2 at 7:30PM CST by NWS San Angelo TX
properties.description:
At 727 PM CST, Doppler radar was tracking strong thunderstorms along
a line extending from near Woodson to near Pumphrey to Grape Creek.
Movement was east at 40 mph.

HAZARD...Wind gusts up to 50 mph and half inch hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Gusty winds could knock down tree limbs and blow around
unsecured objects. Minor hail damage to vegetation is
possible.

Locations impacted include...
Abilene, Ballinger, Clyde, Winters, Albany, Baird, Robert Lee,
Throckmorton, Maverick, Tye, Bronte, Miles, Tuscola, Buffalo Gap,
Lawn, Moran, Woodson, Novice, Putnam, and Ibex.

People attending Dia de Los Muertos at the Abilene Zoo should seek
safe shelter immediately!

This includes Interstate 20 between Mile Markers 275 and 323.
properties.instruction:
Frequent cloud to ground lightning is occurring with these storms.
Lightning can strike 10 miles away from a thunderstorm. Seek a safe
shelter inside a building or vehicle.

These storms may intensify, so be certain to monitor local radio
stations and available television stations for additional information
and possible warnings from the National Weather Service.

A Tornado Watch remains in effect until 1100 PM CST for west central
Texas.

- At 5:00 PM MST Monday the stage was 8.1 feet.

tomorrow morning and continue falling to 4.4 feet late Saturday
morning.

properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in New
Mexico...

Rio Chama Above Abiquiu affecting Rio Arriba County.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Rio Chama above Abiquiu.

* WHEN...Until Tuesday evening.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding impacts are expected along and near the
banks of the Rio Chama.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 5:00 PM MST Monday the stage was 11.3 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 10.2 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 5:00 PM MST Monday was 11.3 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 11.6 feet
late this evening. It will then fall below flood stage late
tomorrow morning.
- Flood stage is 11.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 10.8
feet on 05/09/2009.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/abq.

The next statement will be issued Tuesday morning at 600 AM MST.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued November 2 at 5:39PM MST until November 4 at 5:49PM MST by NWS Albuquerque NM
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in New
Mexico...

San Juan River At Shiprock affecting San Juan County.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and major flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...San Juan River at Shiprock.

* WHEN...Until Wednesday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Significant impacts are likely in the Shiprock area and
along the San Juan River from Shiprock to the Four Corners.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 5:00 PM MST Monday the stage was 18.1 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 13.5 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 5:00 PM MST Monday was 18.1 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 21.3 feet
late tonight. It will then fall below flood stage early Wednesday
morning.
- Flood stage is 15.5 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/abq/EmergencyPrepFlood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Be alert to the forecast and obey all evacuation orders from local
authorities.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/abq.

The next statement will be issued Tuesday morning at 600 AM MST.

evening, however water levels are expected to continue to fall
thereafter.

below flood stage by this evening.

ponding in backwater catch basins.
At 12.0 feet: Nuisance flooding of property along riverbanks.
- For the Verde River near Camp Verde:

Flood Stage is 17.0 feet.
Forecast: A crest of 17.58 feet is expected this evening.
Impacts:
At 17.0 feet: Water begins to flood sites and lower road at Verde
River RV Resort and Cottages.
At 19.0 feet: Flooding begins in Horseshoe Bend area just
upstream of Camp Verde. Several properties and homes begin to
flood along the Verde River downstream in Camp Verde to Beasley
Flat area.

Cottonwood, Camp Verde, Verde Village, Clarkdale, Middle Verde,
Verde Lakes, Mountain View Estates, Childs Power Plant, Dead
Horse Ranch State Park, Tuzigoot National Monument, and Rockin'
River Ranch State Park.

unstable and unsafe during any flooding event.

properties.areaDesc: Coconino, AZ; Navajo, AZ
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued November 2 at 4:44PM MST until November 3 at 10:00AM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...The Little Colorado River from Woodruff to Leupp...

* WHEN...Until 1000 AM MST Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of the Little Colorado River is occurring.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 436 PM MST, water levels have begin to fall near Woodruff and
Holbrook, but both remain above flood stage. Water levels at
Winslow remain above major flood stage, and are expected to rise
through the overnight as elevated flow moves downstream. Flooding
will continue to remain a threat downstream of Winslow in the
Birdsprings area as well. Flooding is already ongoing.
- For the Little Colorado River near Woodruff:
At 4:30pm MST the stage was 21.71 feet.
Flood Stage is 20.5 feet.
Forecast: Water levels have crested and are expected to fall
through this evening.
Impacts:
At 20.5 feet: Bankfull. Portions of residential yards flooded.
- For the Little Colorado River at Holbrook:
Flood Stage is 15.5 feet.
Forecast: A crest of 20.27 feet is expected at 5:00pm MST Monday.
Impacts:
At 15.5 feet: Railroad bridge affected. Overflow on South Bank.
At 25.0 feet: Levee overtopped. Major flooding.
- For the Little Colorado River at Joseph City:
At 4:30pm MST the stage was 6.73 feet.
Flood Stage is 9.0 feet.
Forecast: A crest of 8.09 feet is expected this evening.
Impacts:
At 7.5 feet: Potential downstream lowland overflow.
At 9.0 feet: Flood stage. Minor overflow on right (north) bank,
with no threat to any buildings, mainly rural countryside.
- For the Little Colorado River at Winslow:
At 4:00pm MST the stage was 25.25 feet.
Flood Stage is 19.0 feet.
Forecast: A crest of 39.94 feet is expected at 4:00am MST
Tuesday.
Impacts:
At 22.0 feet: Lowland flooding on right bank. Damage on left bank
to Ames Acres and Bushman Acres in the event of levee failure.
At 25.0 feet: Levee is overtopped. Major flooding of portions of
Winslow including Ames Acres and Bushman Acres.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Winslow, Leupp, Birdsprings, Woodruff, Bushman Acres, Homolovi
Ruins State Park, Rosedale Heights, and Clearview Heights.


- Additional information is available at weather.gov/flagstaff.
properties.instruction:
Move to higher ground now. Act quickly to protect your life.

Stay away or be swept away! The banks of creeks and washes are
unstable and unsafe during any flooding event.

Low water crossings will become dangerous in heavy rain. Do not
attempt to cross flooded roads. Find an alternate route.

late tonight.

direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

properties.areaDesc: Coastal St. Lucie; Coastal Martin
properties.headline: Rip Current Statement issued November 2 at 1:44PM EST until November 4 at 1:00AM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 6
to 7 feet in the surf zone. For the High Rip Current Risk,
dangerous rip currents. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor
coastal flooding.

* WHERE...Coastal Saint Lucie and Coastal Martin Counties.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 3 AM EST Tuesday. For
the High Rip Current Risk, through late Tuesday night. For the
Coastal Flood Advisory, until 7 PM EST Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Some flooding of low-lying lots, parks and roadways
may occur near the shoreline. Only isolated road closures are
expected. Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and
localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best
swimmers away from shore into deeper water.
properties.instruction:
Onshore winds and above normal tides will combine to generate
flooding of low areas along the shore. Do not drive around
barricades or through water of unknown depth. Take the necessary
actions to protect flood-prone property.

High surf will affect the beaches in the advisory area, producing
localized beach erosion and dangerous swimming conditions.
Swimmers should remain out of the water due to large breaking
waves and dangerous surf conditions.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

Entering the surf is strongly discouraged. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

without warning, sweeping people into the sea from rocks,

properties.headline: High Wind Warning issued November 2 at 6:57AM MST until November 2 at 8:00PM MST by NWS Midland/Odessa TX
properties.description:
* WHAT...West winds 30 to 50 mph with gusts up to 70 mph expected.

* WHERE...Guadalupe/Delaware Mountains of west Texas and southeast
New Mexico.

* WHEN...Until 8 PM MST /9 PM CST/ this evening.

* IMPACTS...Travel will be difficult, especially for high profile
vehicles like campers, vans, and tractor trailers. Gusty winds may
blow around unsecured objects. Severe turbulence near the mountains
will be hazardous for low flying light aircraft. Aviation interests
may experience localized but extreme turbulence, or strong downward
airflows if flying in the near the Guadalupe Mountains.
properties.instruction:
Delay travel through Guadalupe Pass or find another route, if
possible.

Use caution if flying low near the mountains as severe turbulence is
possible.

Use caution when driving as blowing dust may reduce visibility.

properties.headline: Beach Hazards Statement issued November 2 at 5:08AM PST until November 3 at 8:00PM PST by NWS San Francisco CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...An increased risk for sneaker waves and strong rip
currents.

* WHERE...Pacific Coast beaches.

* WHEN...Through 8 PM Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Waves can sweep across the shoreline without
warning, pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties,
and rocks.
properties.instruction:
Stay off of jetties, piers, rocks, and other waterside
infrastructure. Remain out of the water to avoid hazardous surf
and NEVER turn your back on the ocean. Monitor local weather,
surf and tide forecasts at www.weather.gov/mtr.

NWSheadline: BEACH HAZARDS STATEMENT REMAINS IN EFFECT THROUGH TUESDAY EVENING

properties.areaDesc: South Central Oregon Coast; Curry County Coast
properties.headline: Beach Hazards Statement issued November 2 at 4:53AM PST until November 2 at 7:00PM PST by NWS Medford OR
properties.description:
* WHAT...A high risk for sneaker waves is expected. A building
west-northwest long period swell is expected to combine with
lower, shorter period northwest and south-southwest swells.

* WHERE...The beaches of Douglas, Coos, and Curry counties.

* WHEN...Through this evening.

* IMPACTS...Sneaker waves can run up significantly farther on
beaches than normal, including over rocks and jetties. These
waves can suddenly knock people off of their feet and sweep
them into the ocean. The waves can also move logs or other
objects which could crush or trap anyone caught underneath.

* View the hazard area in detail at
https://www.wrh.noaa.gov/map/?wfo=mfr
properties.instruction:
Avoid climbing on rocks and jetties. Stay away from the ocean and
remain out of the water to avoid hazardous conditions.

properties.areaDesc: La Plata, CO
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued November 1 at 2:20PM MST until November 2 at 10:00PM MST by NWS Grand Junction CO
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...South Central La Plata County in southwestern Colorado...

* WHEN...Until 1000 PM MST Monday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 218 PM MST, satellite estimates and river gauge data near
Cedar Hill, NM indicate heavy rain in the warned area. Flooding
is ongoing or expected to begin shortly.
- This includes the following streams and drainages...
Animas River, Lightner Creek and Basin Creek.

- At 1:00 PM MST Sunday the stage was 9.5 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage
tonight to a crest of 11.2 feet by early Monday morning. It will
then fall below flood stage Monday night.
- Flood stage is 10.5 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 11.4
feet on 06/19/1949.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Durango and Bondad.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

NWSheadline: FLOOD WARNING IN EFFECT UNTIL 10 PM MST MONDAY

properties.areaDesc: Ventura County Beaches; Malibu Coast; Los Angeles County Beaches
properties.headline: Beach Hazards Statement issued November 1 at 10:29AM PST until November 2 at 6:00PM PST by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerous rip currents and breaking waves due to elevated
surf expected. Minor tidal overflow during high tides.

* WHERE...Ventura County Beaches, Malibu Coast and Los Angeles
County Beaches.

* WHEN...Through Monday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...There is an increased risk of ocean drowning. Rip
currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. Waves can
wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats
nearshore. Minor flood impacts are possible during high tides
with water flowing over normally dry sand and to lower parking
lots or paths. Moderate beach erosion is possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Additional flood impacts are likely into
next weekend with tides reaching 7 ft as early as Friday. Tides
will peak over the weekend into early next week 7.0-7.8 ft.
Elevated surf may increase flood impacts during this time,
especially across west to northwest facing beaches. Reminder,
tides mentioned have been corrected to reflect the most recent
trends in actual tide observations.
properties.instruction:
Remain out of the water due to hazardous swimming conditions, or
stay near occupied lifeguard towers. Rock jetties can be deadly
in such conditions, stay off the rocks.

properties.areaDesc: Archuleta, CO
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued November 1 at 10:09AM MST until November 2 at 7:15PM MST by NWS Grand Junction CO
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...South Central Archuleta County in southwestern Colorado...

* WHEN...Until 715 PM MST Monday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring. Streams
continue to rise due to excess runoff from earlier rainfall.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 959 AM MST, satellite estimates and rain gauge data indicate
heavy rain in the warned area. Flooding is ongoing or expected to
begin shortly.
- This includes the following streams and drainages...
Stove Creek, Navajo River and Little Navajo River.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Chromo.
- At 9:00 AM MST Sunday the stage was 1.2 feet.

Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage this
afternoon to a crest of 8.0 feet this evening. It will then fall
below flood stage early tomorrow afternoon.

Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 5.1.

Http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

Stay away or be swept away. River banks and culverts can become
unstable and unsafe.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.
